description: Distributed systems, architectural scalability, caching, load balancing, and database partitioning.

concepts.name: Load Balancing
concepts.description: Distributing network traffic across multiple servers (L4 vs L7, Round Robin, Consistent Hashing).
concepts.foundational_question: Explain how a Layer 7 load balancer differs from a Layer 4 load balancer. When would you choose one over the other in a high-traffic microservices architecture?
targeted_probes: How does consistent hashing prevent massive cache invalidation when a load-balanced server fails?
What are the trade-offs of using sticky sessions (session affinity) on a Layer 7 load balancer?

rubric.correctness_criteria: Accurately distinguishes L4 (transport/TCP/IP packet level) from L7 (application/HTTP/header/URL level).
rubric.depth_criteria: Explains inspection overhead, SSL termination, and content-based routing mechanics.
rubric.tradeoff_criteria: Analyzes latency/CPU overhead of L7 vs lack of routing intelligence in L4.
rubric.applicability_criteria: Applies to real-world scenarios like path-based routing (/api/v1/auth vs /api/v1/feed) or DDoS mitigation.

learning_resources.title: NGINX & Envoy L7 Architecture Deep Dive

concepts.name: Caching
concepts.description: In-memory caching strategies (Cache-Aside, Write-Through, Write-Back), eviction policies (LRU, LFU), and Cache Stampede prevention.
concepts.foundational_question: Compare the Cache-Aside pattern with the Write-Through caching pattern. How do you handle cache invalidation and prevent cache stampede during high concurrency?
targeted_probes: What happens when a hot key expires in Redis while 10,000 requests per second are requesting it, and how do mutex locks or probabilistic early expiration (XFetch) mitigate this?
What are the consistency trade-offs of Write-Back (Write-Behind) caching during an unexpected cache node crash?

rubric.correctness_criteria: Accurately defines Cache-Aside (app manages read/write to cache & DB) vs Write-Through (cache updates DB synchronously).
rubric.depth_criteria: Explains TTL, eviction strategies (LRU vs LFU), and distributed locking.
rubric.tradeoff_criteria: Identifies eventual consistency risks, write latency vs read latency, and data loss risks in Write-Back.
rubric.applicability_criteria: Provides solutions for Cache Stampede/Thundering Herd (e.g., distributed locks, probabilistic early expiration, background warming).

concepts.name: DB Sharding
concepts.description: Horizontal database partitioning, shard key selection, re-sharding strategies, cross-shard joins, and distributed transactions (2PC/Saga).
concepts.foundational_question: Explain horizontal database sharding. How do you choose an effective Shard Key to avoid hotspotting, and how do you handle cross-shard queries?
targeted_probes: What happens when your user base grows 10x and an existing shard key distribution becomes uneven? How does consistent hashing or directory-based sharding help in re-sharding?
How does the CAP theorem apply when executing distributed transactions across sharded databases, and why is the Saga pattern preferred over Two-Phase Commit (2PC)?

rubric.correctness_criteria: Defines horizontal partitioning (splitting rows across multiple DB instances) vs vertical partitioning.
rubric.depth_criteria: Explains shard key cardinality, hashing algorithms, and scatter-gather query execution.
rubric.tradeoff_criteria: Evaluates cross-shard join complexity, secondary index overhead, and re-sharding operational complexity.
rubric.applicability_criteria: Proposes realistic solutions for hotspotting (e.g., salt/composite keys) and distributed consistency (Saga/Outbox pattern).

learning_resources.title: Practical Distributed Partitioning with PostgreSQL & Citus

concepts.name: Scalability
concepts.description: End-to-end horizontal scaling, stateless architectures, asynchronous event-driven messaging, and resilient fault isolation.
concepts.foundational_question: How do you design a high-throughput event processing architecture that scales gracefully to 100,000 events/sec while guaranteeing at-least-once or exactly-once processing?
targeted_probes: How do consumer groups and partition assignment in message brokers (like Kafka/RabbitMQ) ensure horizontal scale without out-of-order processing?
How do circuit breakers and rate limiters prevent cascading failures in an auto-scaling microservices cluster?

rubric.correctness_criteria: Accurately details decoupling via message brokers, stateless application tiers, and idempotency.
rubric.depth_criteria: Explains partition ordering guarantees, backpressure handling, and graceful degradation.
rubric.tradeoff_criteria: Weighs synchronous REST/gRPC vs asynchronous messaging (Kafka/SQS) and exactly-once processing overhead.
rubric.applicability_criteria: Demonstrates practical resilience patterns (Circuit Breaker, Bulkhead, Exponential Backoff with Jitter).
